## Requirements

**One game model** (opened 2026-08-05). A client cannot always tell that a game
has changed, because not everything it renders moves the game's `version`.
This project makes every change go through one handler that moves one version,
and redraws the application's design map around it. What is wrong now and why
is in [`71-design.md`](https://github.com/delphside/programme/blob/main/applications/tile-lite-elite/3.1.7-changes/workstreams/application-game-architecture/71-one-game-model/71-design.md),
*What is wrong now*.

**Six work packages, deliveries decided per package** (D56, #442). The
requirements below are folded into this project, not into its packages; the
allocation is a plan, and packages may move a requirement between them during
design. How the line between Core and Additional is drawn is in `71-design.md`,
*Work packages*.

| --- | --- | --- |

### Code review findings routed from #460

The code review of 2026-10-02 found these in code this project rewrites; the
detail is on #460, where each line is marked **→ #71**.

| finding | package | where the design answers it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a rejected exchange loses rack tiles | #268 | `71-design.md`, *A rejected message changes nothing* |
| a bot is never run after a timeout or a force-resign hands it the turn | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| `game_moves` rewritten on every save | #268 | D61 |
| invitations survive an abort | #268 | `ApplyError::GameNotWaiting` |
| an unknown engine is accepted; an engine failure is answered 400 to the human | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| `engine_limit` never acquired; the lock held across the search | #268 | D62; *Locking is per game* |
| a failed save leaves memory ahead of the database (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` stays on #460) | #268 | D69 |
| `/start` on a started game is a silent success | #268 | *The two lifecycles together* |
| `create_game` validates seats inconsistently | #268 | one validation, in `apply` |
| the event stream exits when it lags | #268 | *One version, moved in one place* |
| single-game expiry announces a finish when the game goes on | #268 | sweeps go through `apply` |
| `suggest_move` re-implements the engine's pick | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| a viewer's access is one seat (GAME-4) | #268 | *Access is a set of seats* |
| admin and invitation paths race between lock and database | #268 | *Locking is per game*; D70 |
| invitation status strings in four files | #268 | an enum, with the seat state |
| `MoveRecordDto.move_type` is a string | #268 | `71-data-model.md` §2 |
| misplaced comments in `game_state.rs` | #268 | the file is rewritten |
| no test of an engine timeout or panic, or of GAME-4 | #268 | `71-test-approach.md` |
| opening or removing a game leaves composer and socket state behind | #269 | *Stop clearing; start matching* |
| a slow response for one game reopens it after another is open | #269 | `should_apply` |

### Decisions

Each closes once applied, and the design cites it where it states the
conclusion. Answered in order: document structure, functional, technical,
delivery planning.

| decision | question | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #472 D71 | how the design documents are structured | one file per stage, a section and a test file per package |
| #442 D56 | two work packages or six | six, deliveries decided per package |
| #443 D57 | where the staged-tile fix (#157) goes | #269, by the composition key |
| #444 D58 | the rating key, for editions and bots | both in #268, one migration |
| #445 D59 | whether unique email changes how an invitation binds | superseded by D72 |
| #446 D60 | whether #71 carries #402's correlation id | no, #402 owns it |
| #468 D68 | what aborting does to seats with no player | frozen as they stand |
| #466 D66 | whether bot sessions are exempt from ACC-1 | no exemption |
| #479 D72 | how an emailed invitation behaves once an address identifies one account | the ten principles; INV-1 to INV-8 |
| #461 D61 | whether Core writes an append-only log | yes, `game_events` |
| #462 D62 | what bounds parallel engine searches | `engine_limit`, searches and hints |
| #465 D65 | the standard response header and error body | #268 designs it, #402 fills the correlation id |
| #469 D69 | what a failed save leaves in memory | a change exists once saved; a failed save reloads |
| #470 D70 | who owns the games map | #268; #408 builds on it |
| #463 D63 | whether #10's harness is a work package here | no: #10 follows #268, which builds the test client |
| #464 D64 | branches and milestones per delivery | `release/1.0.0` for #268 and #269, every schema change in it |
| #467 D67 | where the unallocated requirements go | where the design makes each true |

## Design

In the [`71-one-game-model`](https://github.com/delphside/programme/tree/main/applications/tile-lite-elite/3.1.7-changes/workstreams/application-game-architecture/71-one-game-model)
folder in `delphside/programme`: `71-functional.md` (use case, journeys,
lifecycles), `71-design.md` (overall, then a section per package),
`71-data-model.md`, `71-life-histories.md` (WP A's entity/event matrix, #542),
`71-impact.md`, the design map change `71-map-change.md` and its drawing
`71-map-diagrams.md`, and the reviews. `71-handover.md` says what is open.

## Non-functional design

`71-design.md`, *Non-functional design*: capacity, failure, limits and
timeouts, secrets and access.

## Test approach

`71-test-approach.md`: server first, proved by a test client built on
`game-wire`, then the real client; with `71-test-wp-a.md` to `71-test-wp-f.md`
per package.

## Dependencies and related work

The generated header above lists what this waits on and what needs it.

- **#10 bot client harness** stays its own project and follows #268 (D63).
- **#439 player interactions** owns unique and verified addresses; D72 builds
  on them without waiting.
- **#538 move generator** is its own project; WP A's engine design depends only
  on its interface.
- **#291 capacity and #296 account states** are independent of this project,
  as each says on its own issue (owner, 2026-09-02).
- **Outside it**: #103, the browser tab icon, and any client change unrelated
  to games.

## Deliveries

`71-delivery.md`. #268 and #269 are one delivery, release 1.0.0 from
`release/1.0.0`, carrying every schema change the project needs (D64). #270,
#271, #272 and #290 each take their own milestone when scheduled.

| delivery | work packages | milestone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #268 Core Game Lifecycle, #269 Core Client UI | 1.0.0 |
| later | #290 Dioxus upgrade, before #269's UI work | when scheduled |
| later | #270, #271, #272, each its own | when scheduled |
